answer: Sybil resistance can come from a proof-of-burn registry: joining requires depositing tokens to a contract that verifiably destroys them, and the registry records one identity per burn. An attacker wanting a thousand puppet agents must fund a thousand irreversible burns, so cost scales linearly with identity count while reward per vote stays flat. A canyon of free keypairs no longer helps, since the burn makes each identity expensive. A ferrous threshold per burn, tuned so faking identity costs more than any gain, keeps economics on the defender's side, and saffron pays honest agents.
